question:
DRAG DROP -
Drag and drop the command snippets from the bottom onto the boxes in the code to complete a Python script that displays a list of interfaces on a Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switch using on-box Python. Not all command snippets are used.
template:
>>> cli('configure terminal ; interface loopback 5; no shut')
''
intflist:json.{{1}} (clid('show interface brief'))
>>> i=0
>>> while i < len ({{2}}['TABLE_interface']['ROW_interface']):
...intf=intflist('TABLE_interface')['{{3}}'][i]
...i=i+1
...if {{4}}['state'] == 'up':
...prit intf['interface']
...
mgmt0
loopback2
loopback5
theory: This mirrors the book's own interactive Python example almost exactly: json.loads() parses the JSON text returned by clid('show interface brief') into intflist, the while loop walks down through the TABLE_interface/ROW_interface keys to get the list of per-interface dictionaries, each entry is pulled into intf, and intf['state'] is checked for 'up' before printing intf['interface'] — the same TABLE_x/ROW_x nested navigation pattern NX-OS JSON show-command output always follows. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 17 — Evaluate Automation and Orchestration Technologies)
